claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, let me ask: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 and still lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is over 16, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in college, sixth form, doing A-levels, or enrolled in an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is studying for his A-levels, that counts as approved education.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask: **Does Alex work, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: **Are you currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim? And is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I haven't claimed it before. And no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✅ **Alex qualifies** - Even though he's 18, you can still claim Child Benefit for him because he's under 20 and in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form college)

✅ **You meet the responsibility criteria** - Alex lives at home with you in the UK, so you're responsible for him

✅ **No disqualifying factors** - Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week and isn't receiving benefits in his own right

✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Important things to note:**

- Child Benefit will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20 years old
- If Alex starts working 24 hours or more per week, starts an apprenticeship, or starts receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit, you would need to inform HMRC as this would affect your eligibility
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can now proceed with making your claim for Child Benefit for Alex!
